1160	And it came to pass one day, that despite all this, one of
1161	the sons, who had brought Dad tefillin,
1162	it became clear at the last moment that they were Rabbeinu Tam's, and it was changed at the last moment because of Dad's question.
1163	And indeed Dad caught it at the last moment and did not bless, and they switched it for him to Rashi's before Rabbeinu Tam's.
1164	But there was a somewhat more internal case, that on one of the occasions
1165	when the son was already used to this question, and answered automatically, "Yes, yes, it's Rashi, yes, yes, it's Rabbeinu Tam."
1166	A mistake came out, and Dad made the blessing over Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin.
1167	And afterwards: "Oh, what did I do?"
1168	The son came and apologized.
1169	Then came the consolations: it is written in the holy books that every person will have it happen
1170	once in his life, that he will err and bless over Rabbeinu Tam's
1171	before Rashi's. Once in his life it will happen to him. So it is brought in the book Taamei HaMinhagim, which says
1172	a tradition from holy men: the man who is careful all his days to put on Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin and never lacks, in
1173	all his days, due to any circumstance, it must be that it will happen to him once to bless over Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin
1174	with the blessings, and to pray in them.
1175	He also brings there from the book Yakar Tosefta, written by a kabbalist in the name of Rabbi Mordechai of Dvorna,
1176	that Rabbeinu Tam effected in the heavenly court that whoever puts on Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin will have it happen to him at the very least, once
1177	in his life, that he will err and put on, with a blessing, Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin instead of Rashi's tefillin.
1178	And that there is such a tradition in the name of the holy Rav of Lublin, and afterwards he brings more books there, and so on.
1179	In any case, for our purposes, even the mistake that happened to my father was done by deliberate providence
1180	from Heaven, because so it needed to be, since Rabbeinu Tam asked in Heaven that whoever it may be,
1181	once will come to an error,
1182	so that he will get to bless and pray with Rabbeinu Tam's tefillin.
1183	But our father was meticulous, very meticulous, between man and his fellow, between man
1184	and the Almighty, especially in monetary matters.
1185	For several years he would receive in the mail a calendar, the
1186	Or HaChaim calendar of the Or HaChaim yeshiva in Jerusalem; they would send it to him by mail every year.
1187	Right away our father would sit, that very day he would sit, and send them back
1188	an envelope with payment. Once we asked him:
1189	Why do they send it to you, and why do you pay for what you didn't even ask for, and we already have a calendar
1190	at home? He answered that apparently once I donated to them,
1191	and since then they send it to me regularly. Since they go to the trouble of sending, and also enclose an envelope
1192	for return payment, they expect to receive, so I don't change from what I did
1193	at the beginning, the first time. And so he continued to pay for the calendar even though he owed them nothing; he hadn't asked
1194	that they send it to him again, but if they already send it and have grown accustomed, then I continue too,
1195	yes, with what I did the first time. Care in monetary matters, care
1196	in his own monetary matters, regarding another's, yes?
1197	A person is called a tzaddik who is careful in monetary matters. Noach ish tzaddik.
1198	Our Sages tell us, the Gemara says: a tzaddik in money.
1199	As we produced a comprehensive lesson on the topic, entitled "Ish Tzaddik."
